issues.legal_issue: The presumption of correctness attaching to a later land-revenue entry can be rebutted by evidence that the entry was changed mistakenly or without authority and without material justifying the change.
material_facts: Earlier land records showed the relevant shares distributed among descendants of three family branches.
Later records showed only descendants of one branch as entitled to the disputed common land.
There was no mutation or order of a revenue authority authorizing the change, and the evidence supported the finding that the later entries had been made mistakenly.
issues.conclusion: The presumption in favour of the later entries was rebutted, and the High Court was right to uphold the decree based on the earlier entries.
issues.legal_principle: Section 44 of the Punjab Land Revenue Act, 1887 gives revenue entries a rebuttable presumption of correctness. Under Shri Raja Durga Singh of Solan v. Tholu, a later substituted entry ordinarily prevails over an earlier entry and enjoys that presumption unless it is established to be wrong or is superseded. The Court agreed that evidence of an unauthorized or mistaken alteration, with no material justifying it, rebutted the presumption in this case.

rule.if: land_revenue_entry_dispute and later_entry_conflicts_with_earlier and later_entry_lacks_authorized_basis and evidence_supports_mistake_or_unsupported_change

predicates.land_revenue_entry_dispute: The dispute concerns entitlement shown in land-revenue records.
predicates.later_entry_conflicts_with_earlier: A later land-revenue entry records entitlement differently from an earlier entry.
predicates.later_entry_lacks_authorized_basis: No competent authority order or recorded mutation supports the change in the later entry.
predicates.evidence_supports_mistake_or_unsupported: The evidence supports that the change was mistaken or had no material basis.

issues.definition: When a land-revenue dispute involves a conflicting later entry that lacks an authorized basis and the evidence supports a mistaken or unsupported change, the presumption attached to that later entry is rebutted.

issues.legal_issue: A claim of adverse possession that was not pleaded in the written statement cannot be raised for the first time at the appellate stage.
material_facts: The defendants had not based their written statement on adverse possession.
They sought to rely on their long possession only at the appellate stage.
issues.conclusion: The adverse-possession claim could not be raised at that stage.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the procedural principle that a party cannot introduce at the appellate stage a defence that was not made the basis of its written statement. No statutory provision or earlier case was cited for this point.

predicates.civil_possession_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal in a civil claim concerning possession.
predicates.adverse_possession_not_pleaded: The party did not set out adverse possession as a basis of its defence in the written statement.
predicates.adverse_possession_raised_at_appellate_s: The party sought to rely on adverse possession only during the appellate proceedings.

issues.definition: In a civil possession appeal, an adverse-possession claim is not entertained when it was omitted from the written statement and raised only during the appeal.
